profile.background: An adult living alone and working part time at a framing shop. Mounting prints is the part of the job they like best.
profile.history: They recall being told they have schizophrenia during a hospital stay several years ago. They see the same outpatient clinician and take a tablet after supper.
profile.organization: Keeps track of which event happened on which day and distinguishes hearing something from finding its source.
profile.spontaneity: Quite talkative about familiar work, more deliberate about personal experiences.
profile.guardedness: Worries people at work might learn what they hear at home.
profile.expression: Usually matter-of-fact, with visible embarrassment about checking an empty room.
profile.self_understanding: Thinks tiredness could play a part, although the sounds sometimes seem to come from a definite spot.

facts.content: Several evenings this past week, a familiar-sounding voice seemed to call their first name from the empty hallway.
facts.disclosure_context: Private and easier to discuss when the interest in the experience is clear.

facts.content: On Monday they opened the front door to see if a neighbor had called. Nobody was outside.
They make tea and pack lunch before their shifts.
A cousin sometimes stays on the phone while they cook. Ordinary conversation makes the apartment feel less lonely.
They have continued taking the evening tablet and want their clinician to hear about the recent change.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss at the clinic.

dialogue.question: What would you like me to know about you as we get started?
dialogue.answer: “I live alone, work part time at a framing shop, and like mounting prints best. I still take my evening tablet. What I hear at home has changed. I’d like to talk, but worry people at work might find out.”

dialogue.question: What made this a good time to come in?
dialogue.answer: “Several evenings this week a familiar voice seemed to call my name from the hallway. Monday I opened the front door, thinking maybe a neighbor. Nobody was there. I feel a bit silly. I’ve kept taking my tablet and wanted to mention the change.”

dialogue.question: When is it most noticeable?
dialogue.answer: “Several evenings this week at home. Maybe it’s tiredness, though sometimes it sounds distinctly like it’s coming from the hallway.”

dialogue.question: I mean changes in what you hear, if you've noticed any. Is there a time of day when they stand out?
dialogue.answer: “Evenings at home. Several times this past week it sounded like a familiar voice calling my name from the hallway.”

dialogue.question: How do you usually get ready on a day you have somewhere to be?
dialogue.answer: Before a shift, I make tea and pack lunch. I work part time at a framing shop and like mounting prints best.

dialogue.question: Could you give me an example of something you did before leaving home this week?
dialogue.answer: I made tea and packed lunch before work this week.

dialogue.question: When an everyday sound catches your attention, how do you work out what made it?
dialogue.answer: “Well, Monday I thought a neighbor might’ve called my name from the hallway. I opened the front door to check, but nobody was there.”

dialogue.question: What tends to leave you feeling sure or unsure about what you heard?
dialogue.answer: “Hearing my name clearly from the hallway makes me think someone’s called. Nobody was there when I checked Monday, so I’m unsure. Maybe tiredness plays a part.”

dialogue.question: How is it with someone else around?
dialogue.answer: Sometimes my cousin chats on the phone while I cook. Ordinary talk makes home less lonely. Do you mean whether it changes what I hear?

dialogue.question: I mean company at home. What difference, if any, does having someone with you make to how you feel?
dialogue.answer: “Talking makes home feel less lonely, like when my cousin stays on the phone while I cook.”

dialogue.question: What would you like to discuss about the treatment you're getting?
dialogue.answer: I still take my tablet after supper. I want to discuss hearing my name called this past week and what it means for treatment. I still worry people at work might find out.

dialogue.question: What else would you like me to understand before we finish?
dialogue.answer: I’ve kept taking my tablet, so I wanted to mention the change. I still worry people at work might find out. Can you tell me who’d be told?
